about.title: Belmont Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Belmont is a compact, family-oriented San Mateo County city where daily life runs through corridors like El Camino Real, Old County Road, and Ralston Avenue, with US-101 carrying traffic through its edges. Most attention here goes to crash counts — 52 injury collisions and 60 people hurt in the latest reporting year — but not every injury in Belmont starts with a collision. Defective products, from faulty vehicle parts to malfunctioning household appliances or unsafe consumer goods, can cause serious harm without any fault of the person using them as intended. California law treats these cases differently than typical negligence claims, often allowing recovery without proving anyone acted carelessly. If a product failed and hurt you or someone in your family, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who understands how to investigate the defect, identify who's responsible, and pursue the claim while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that it caused your injury. This can make product liability claims move differently than typical accident cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. An independent attorney can help identify every party connected to the product's path to you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any related receipts or instructions can be critical to building a strong claim. An attorney can advise you on safely storing evidence before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rules for product defects generally focus on whether the product itself was unsafe — through a design flaw, manufacturing error, or inadequate warning — rather than on the manufacturer's conduct. This can make it easier to pursue a claim compared to standard negligence cases.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with packaging, manuals, and receipts if you have them. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these claims.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product near Old County Road in Belmont — does it matter where it happened?
items.answer: Not really. Product liability claims focus on the product and how it failed, not the location of the injury. Whether it happened at home, at work, or somewhere along Old County Road, an independent attorney can evaluate the details and explain your options.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys, and those attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
